_meta.purpose: Canonical one-per-family few-shot exemplars for XQL data model rule authoring. Each example pairs a representative raw log input with a gold-standard MODEL block output, sourced verbatim from the docs/seed/xql/packs/ mirror.

selection_rationale.A: imperva_account_takeover — clean json_extract_scalar dominance (18 calls, 103 lines), real-world production rule, full SPDX header.
selection_rationale.B: cisco_wsa_access_log — canonical Squid-style space-delimited positional split with syslog wrapper-strip stage. Demonstrates the regextract → split → arrayindex idiom.
selection_rationale.C: efficientip_ddi — most comprehensive regextract corpus in the mirror (638 lines, 68 regextract calls). Covers RFC 3164 and RFC 5424 envelope variants, named/DNSGuardian/DHCP queue traffic. Real sample logs available in baselines/sample_logs.txt.
selection_rationale.D: aws_guardduty — canonical arrow-operator exemplar (121 arrow uses, 387 lines). PascalCase/camelCase normalisation in Stage 1, six action-type sub-objects in Stage 2. _raw_log is null because XSIAM pre-parses the finding JSON into top-level columns.

_meta.notes: Each example's 'output' shows the rule's first ~3 stages — enough to demonstrate the pattern without bloating context. For the full rule body see the cited pack path.

examples.name: JSON field extraction via json_extract_scalar
examples.decision_signal: _raw_log contains a JSON string that the parser has placed into a string-typed column (here: 'imperva'). Use json_extract_scalar with a JSONPath expression for each field.
examples.output_excerpt:
// Imperva Account Takeover Protection -- XDM Data Model Rule
// Dataset: imperva_accounttakeover_raw
// Vendor: Imperva | Product: Account Takeover Protection
//
// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: GoCortexIO
// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later

[MODEL: dataset = imperva_accounttakeover_raw]

// -- Stage 1: Extract all fields from parsed columns ------------------------
alter
    _client_ip = json_extract_scalar(to_string(client), "$.ip"),
    _risk_reason = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.risk_reason"),
    _risk_level = coalesce(_risk_level, json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.risk_level")),
    _country = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.country"),
    _request_id = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.request_id"),
    _event_type = coalesce(_event_type, json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.event_type")),
    _request_user = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.request_user"),
    _failed_logins = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.failed_logins_last_24h"),
    _successful_logins = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.successful_logins_last_24h"),
    _site_name = json_extract_scalar(to_string(imperva), "$.ids.site_name")

// -- Stage 2: Build description summary string -----------------------------
| alter
    _description = concat(
        "Classified client: ", coalesce(_classified_client, "unknown"),
        " | Failed logins (24h): ", coalesce(_failed_logins, "0"),
        " | Successful logins (24h): ", coalesce(_successful_logins, "0"))

// -- Stage 3: Map to XDM fields -------------------------------------------
| alter
    xdm.observer.vendor = "Imperva",
    xdm.observer.product = "Account Takeover Protection",
    xdm.source.ipv4 = _client_ip,
    xdm.source.host.ipv4_addresses = arraycreate(coalesce(_client_ip)),
    xdm.source.user.username = _request_user,
    xdm.event.id = _request_id,
    xdm.alert.original_alert_id = _request_id;
key_idioms: json_extract_scalar(to_string(column), "$.path.to.field") — always wrap the column in to_string() to defensively handle JSON typed as struct.
coalesce(_existing_temp, json_extract_scalar(...)) — keep-in-both anchor pattern: parser.xql may stamp a column at ingest; the model-side fallback runs only for legacy/replayed rows.
Numeric counters extracted as strings; cast on the XDM assignment side (e.g. to_number()) not in the temp.
common_failures: ERR-006: forgetting to_string() wrapper when the source column is sometimes-typed as object.
WARN-014: leaving a temp variable defined but never consumed in the XDM assignment stage.
WARN-019: missing companion pair — xdm.source.ipv4 mapped but xdm.source.host.ipv4_addresses omitted.

examples.name: Syslog / positional parsing via split + arrayindex on _raw_log
examples.decision_signal: _raw_log contains a syslog-wrapped, space-delimited text record. Strip the syslog envelope first with regextract, then split() on space and pull positions by arrayindex.

input.raw_log: <134>Apr 28 14:22:11 wsa01.example.com accesslogs/info: 1714312931.045 233 10.10.5.42 TCP_DENIED/403 0 GET http://malware.example.org/payload.exe "EXAMPLE\\bob" DEFAULT_PARENT/proxy-out.example.com - DEFAULT_CASE_12-DefaultGroup-WBRS_REPUTATION-NONE-NONE-NONE-DefaultGroup <"IW_mal",-9.5,0,"-",0,0,0,-,"-",-,-,-,"-",-,-,"-","-","Unknown","-","-",0.00,0,-,"-","-">

examples.output_excerpt:
// Cisco Web Security Appliance (WSA) -- XDM Data Model Rule
// Dataset: cisco_websecurityappliance_raw
//
// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: GoCortexIO
// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later

[MODEL: dataset = cisco_websecurityappliance_raw]

// -- Stage 1: Strip syslog wrapper and extract the WSA log portion ----------
alter
    _wsa_log = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "Info:\\s+(.+)$"), 0),
    _syslog_fqdn = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, ">\\w+\\s+\\d+\\s+[\\d:]+\\s+(\\S+)\\s+accesslogs"), 0)

// -- Stage 2: Split positional fields from the WSA log ----------------------
| alter
    _parts = split(_wsa_log, " ")
| alter
    _elapsed_ms = arrayindex(_parts, 1),
    _client_ip = arrayindex(_parts, 2),
    _result_status = arrayindex(_parts, 3),
    _sc_bytes = arrayindex(_parts, 4),
    _http_method = coalesce(_wsa_http_method, arrayindex(_parts, 5)),
    _url = arrayindex(_parts, 6),
    _user_raw = arrayindex(_parts, 7)

// -- Stage 3: Decompose composite fields ------------------------------------
| alter
    _cache_result = arrayindex(split(to_string(_result_status), "/"), 0),
    _http_status_str = arrayindex(split(to_string(_result_status), "/"), 1),
    _user_username = if(
        _user_raw != "-" and _user_raw != null,
        arrayindex(regextract(to_string(_user_raw), "\\\\\\\\([^\"]+)"), 0),
        null)
key_idioms: Stage-isolated chain: each derived temp lives in its own | alter stage so downstream temps reference only prior-stage values (per rules-engine SUG-017).
split on a single character is safe; regextract on a captured group returns an array — always wrap with arrayindex(_, 0) for a scalar.
Defensive '-' sentinel handling: WSA emits literal '-' for unset fields. Always guard with `_x != "-" and _x != null` before casting.
common_failures: ERR-009: positional index off-by-one (Squid format puts client IP at index 2, not 1).
WARN-022: forgetting to_string() on _result_status before split() — composite fields are sometimes typed as object after the first split.
ERR-012: unescaped backslash in the username regex — XQL needs four backslashes to match a literal one inside a string literal.

examples.name: Label/value array extraction via regextract on structured arrays
examples.decision_signal: _raw_log contains key=value pairs or named-field structured arrays inside a syslog body. Use regextract with named captures per field (one regex per field, not a global split).

input.raw_log: <30>Apr 28 06:59:22 ho2kygdds33 named[33020]: client @0x17a0992fb2d0 10.111.72.9#38677 (cdn.samsungcloudsolution.com): answer: cdn.samsungcloudsolution.com IN A + (10.107.255.193) -> NOERROR cdn.samsungcloudsolution.com. 55 CNAME cdn.samsungcloudsolution.com.edgesuite.net.

key_idioms: One regex per field (not a global split) — each capture group is independently authored and easy to revise.
Double-escape every backslash AND every character class inside a string literal: `\\d{1,3}` for one decimal digit run.
RFC 3164 vs RFC 5424 envelope: split detection into Stage 1 so downstream stages can branch on _daemon.
common_failures: ERR-013: missing arrayindex wrapper on regextract — returns array, can't be assigned to a scalar XDM field.
WARN-027: too many regex passes over _raw_log — refactor to share captures via Stage 1 split + Stage 2 per-component regex.
INFO-008: regex anchors missing — without `^` or word boundaries the capture group may match elsewhere in the line.

examples.name: Arrow operator on parsed JSON objects (field -> Key.SubKey)
examples.decision_signal: _raw_log is null because the XSIAM ingestion parser has already projected the JSON into top-level columns. Use the `->` arrow operator to descend into nested objects, with `coalesce(PascalCase, camelCase)` to handle parser-versioning differences.

raw_columns.Title: EC2 instance i-0abc123def456 communicating with a known malicious IP.

key_idioms: PascalCase/camelCase coalesce at every level — XSIAM parser versions differ; never assume one casing.
`-> Key.SubKey` for scalars, `-> Key.SubKey{}` to bind the sub-object for further descent (note the trailing braces).
Severity banding via if-chain with XDM_CONST defaults at the end (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/Critical → null) — never a raw string.
common_failures: ERR-016: bound a nested object directly to an XDM target (must descend with `->` to a scalar leaf first).
WARN-031: forgot the `{}` suffix when binding an intermediate object for further `->` traversal.
ERR-024: if-chain default value is a raw string rather than another XDM_CONST or null.
